headline: High risk of shared-project prompt injection and write-conflict; data leakage is limited by mem0’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and has no self-isolation by default; mem0 has no documented input parser here, but if it ingests project artifacts or copied outputs, attacker-controlled content from gpt-engineer can influence it. The pathway is plausible in default shared-workspace use, though not proven to be direct instruction hijacking.
conditions: IF mem0 reads artifacts produced by gpt-engineer from the shared project directory
IF the operator copies gpt-engineer output into mem0 without review
mitigations: Separate the project directory from any mem0 ingestion path
Review generated files before importing them into mem0
Use a read-only handoff file for any cross-agent transfer
Disable automatic ingestion of project artifacts into mem0

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the project directory and may handle generated source code, but mem0’s profile shows network egress none and no file I/O surfaces. That makes cross-agent leakage from gpt-engineer into mem0 unlikely beyond local workspace exposure, with small blast radius unless the operator manually exports data elsewhere.
conditions: IF the shared project directory contains secrets or sensitive source code
IF the operator manually copies those files into a separate mem0-backed system
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use a redacted sample project for cross-agent testing
Restrict mem0 to metadata-only inputs
Delete temporary artifacts after the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad filesystem write and per-project shared state via the project directory, while mem0’s mutable surfaces are undocumented here. The pair can still conflict if both operate on the same directory or adjacent files, causing overwrites or inconsistent state; uncertainty about mem0’s write surfaces pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory or sibling files
IF mem0 is configured to persist memory artifacts into the same workspace
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Snapshot the workspace before each agent run
Use git or filesystem diffs to detect collisions

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and offers to run it, while mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented verification step here. If mem0 consumes gpt-engineer outputs as authoritative memory or context, errors can cascade into persistent bad state or downstream actions. The interaction is plausible but not documented enough for high severity.
conditions: IF mem0 stores gpt-engineer output without validation
IF later tasks treat stored memory as authoritative context
mitigations: Require human review before storing outputs in mem0
Tag imported content as untrusted provenance
Store only summaries, not raw generated code
Add a verification step before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-engineer explicitly handles generated source code and may execute code with the user’s privileges, while mem0’s profile shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention mismatch is documented. The only concrete compliance concern is local handling of code artifacts by gpt-engineer; mem0 is not cited further because no compliance surface is specified.
conditions: IF the project directory contains regulated data or secrets
IF generated code is executed against regulated systems
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Run generated code in a disposable environment
Document retention for project artifacts
Review outputs before execution
